newsitem.title: EGYPT: RESEARCH ALERT - Alexandria Flour Mills starts as "buy up to $25".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Alexandria Flour Mills starts as "buy up to $25".

text.p: London-based brokers T. Hoare and Co. said on Tuesday Alexandria Flour Mills, a firm the Egyptian state has recently put up for privatisation, was the best-valued stock in the milling sector.
The state offered investors up to 30 percent of Alexandria Flour Mill's total four million shares at an initial price of 75 pounds per share. The offer closed on Monday.

An official at Commercial International Investment Company, one of the agents for the privatisation, said brokers were still processing investors' bids but he estimated the offer was initially more than five times oversubscribed.
T. Hoare recommended investors buy the stock at a price of up to 85 pounds ($25) and the official said the bidding price in the orders processed so far ranged from 80 to 85 pounds.

The brokerage firm said in a faxed statement it had based its recommendation on the new management of Alexandria Flour Mills, cost cutting and efficiency measures and an expectation that earnings in 1997 would increase by 140 percent.
"The firm covers the Alexandria, northern coast and Western Desert regions... the most dynamic and affluent economic growth areas in Egypt," the statement said.

T. Hoare forecast net profits for Alexandria Flour Mills would rise to 43.28 million pounds in the 1997/8 fiscal year, which began on July 1, from 32.84 million in the previous 1996/7 year, which ended on June 30.
The brokers also said Alexandria Flour Mills was constructing four new mills, including the first disk mill in the Middle East, which would increase the firm's revenue by 25 million pounds.
The state has also sold 10 percent of the firm to its employees.
